text.p: Swedish police said on Sunday that neo-Nazi demonstrations to commemorate the death of an eighteenth century king regarded as a nationalist hero had resulted in one person being stabbed and several arrests.

Police said several hundred skinheads had gathered in Atvidaberg, 150 km (95 miles) south of Stockholm, and at Simrishman on the south coast to mark the death of Karl XII, regarded as a hero by a growing number of Swedish neo-Nazis.
Police spokesman Stig Persson told the national news agency TT that one person had been arrested for assault after fighting broke out at the demonstration in Atvidaberg. He was later released.
One skinhead was taken to hospital with stab wounds after a fight with a rival gang in Stockholm on Saturday night. Police said two people had been arrested.

The weekend closest to the anniversary of Karl's death on November 30 has become a focal point in recent years for Swedish neo-Nazis. Their numbers have grown rapidly in the past two years and there has been a rise in racist incidents reported to police.
Karl XII became king of Sweden in 1697. A brave but rash general, he was responsible for the loss of the Swedish empire which at that time spread across much of the Baltic.
He remains a revered figure for his efforts, often suicidal, to defend Sweden which included marching on Russia.
Police estimate there is a hard core of up to 1,000 neo-Nazis in Sweden. There are also several thousand sympathisers.
